subject: Clarification: default capture, ephemeral boundaries, and erasure runbook for BrightBank
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: sec-questions@brightbank.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarification: default capture, ephemeral boundaries, and erasure runbook for BrightBank

Alan / BrightBank team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. I promised a short follow-up that lays out the default treatment we apply to different interaction elements and the practical erasure path if you need records removed or need proof of deletion. I attached the RB_Security_FAQ_v2.pdf and a simple data-flow image for context.

Quick summary up front (see full answers below):
- Default hosted capture windows: requests (raw user input) stored 30 days; model outputs (final generations) retained 90 days; streaming fragments ephemeral up to 24 hours for session continuity.
- Customers can opt out of capture or request erasure via the Console or Support runbook; typical SLA for deletion evidence is 10 business days.

Things I want you to confirm so we provide the right artifacts:
1) Does BrightBank need retention buckets pinned to 0 days for any environment (i.e., never stored)?
2) Do you need residency (logs kept only in eu vs us) beyond the standard regional tenant controls we discussed?

If helpful, Ben will paste the short runbook and a Drive link showing the deletion evidence template.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RB_Security_FAQ_v2.pdf (pdf), redwood-data-flow-diagram.png (png)

From: BrightBank Security <sec-questions@brightbank.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightbank.com, alan.wu@brightbank.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarification: default capture, ephemeral boundaries, and erasure runbook for BrightBank

Kimberly — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. A few follow-ups from our InfoSec and Procurement teams so we can close the DPA questions: 

1) Can you confirm exact definitions you use for: 
   - "request/raw input" vs "prompt" (we need the canonical names for the contract)
   - "model output" vs "derived artifact"

2) For outputs that are kept 90 days by default: can those be set to 0 (never stored) per-account, and is that a self-serve toggle or an account engagement with support?

3) What form does "proof of deletion" take? We require a time-stamped artifact and a checksum or similar.

4) Residency: we're EU-headquartered; our legal team wants confirmation that logs for EU tenants remain in-region and are not replicated to non-EU telemetry stores by default.

Also: Procurement asked whether you can provide the erasure SLA in writing (max time to complete and to provide evidence).

Appreciate the quick turn — Alan will coordinate with Procurement if we need a formal change order.

— BrightBank Security

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarification: default capture, ephemeral boundaries, and erasure runbook for BrightBank

Hi Alan / team —

I dropped a compact runbook into the Drive folder linked below that shows the self-serve options in Console and the Support path (when you need certified proof of deletion). Short notes:
- Per-account toggles: you can set "capture off" for hosted API keys from the Console; turning it off prevents new request/response payloads from being stored going forward but does not retroactively delete prior records without a separate erasure request.
- Region residency: for EU tenants we default to EU region stores; replication to other regions is off by default unless you enable cross-region backups.
- Erasure evidence: we produce a signed deletion manifest with timestamps and SHA-256 checksums for exported blobs.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExample
DocuSign: DocuSign envelope 0A7B8C (DPA)

If you want, we can schedule a short call to walk Procurement through the deletion manifest format.

Thanks —
Ben
Account Director, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: sec-questions@brightbank.com, procurement@brightbank.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarification: default capture, ephemeral boundaries, and erasure runbook for BrightBank

Alan / team —

Below are the concrete defaults and the operational steps so you have language to include in your security questionnaire and DPA redline: please feel free to copy/paste.

Policy definitions (canonical names we use internally and in the Console):
- "Request (raw_input)": the original text bytes received from a client call (what customers typically call the "prompt").
- "Streaming fragment": short-lived tokenized buffers used for live sessions; kept up to 24 hours solely for session continuity and then purged automatically.
- "Model output (generation)": the final returned completion(s) produced by the model; treated as a derived artifact.
- "KV/Cache tombstones": internal inference cache metadata retained up to 7 days to enable retry/resume flows.

Default retention windows (hosted / unmodified account):
- Requests (raw_input): 30 days. Collected for telemetry, safety monitoring, and model quality.
- Model outputs (generated responses): 90 days. Kept to enable troubleshooting and customer support investigations; flagged derivatives are accessible to the tenant via the Console export during that window.
- Streaming fragments: up to 24 hours (ephemeral) unless explicitly saved by the integration.
- KV/cache artifacts: up to 7 days.

Opt-outs and account-level controls:
- Capture toggle in Console: self-serve. When enabled to OFF, new inbound requests are not stored. This does not automatically remove historical captures — for that, file an erasure request (see below).
- Per-model/route pinning: customers can request that particular routes never persist outputs. This is typically a supported configuration we provision for production accounts (requires change request).

Erasure and evidence process (operational runbook):
1) Submit erasure request via Console or Support with the account id, time window, and artifact types (requests/outputs). Use the template attached (erasure-request-template.docx).
2) Support validates scope and schedules a purge job. SLA: 10 business days to complete purge for standard requests; 3 business days for emergency (with signed exception).
3) After purge, we provide a signed Deletion Manifest (timestamped) listing blobs removed with SHA-256 checksums and an internal job id. That manifest is retained for 2 years for audit purposes and can be shared with the customer.

Residency notes: 
- EU customers on a regional tenant: logs and artifacts remain in-region by default and are not replicated to non-EU telemetry stores unless cross-region backup is explicitly enabled by the customer.
- For Dedicated/Private deployments: residency follows the customer's infrastructure boundaries.

Security controls and safeguards:
- PII: Fields explicitly marked as PII in the Console are redacted in analytics stores by default; full raw inputs are still available in the tenant's export unless Capture is turned off.
- Access: Internal operations access to audio/text artifacts requires two-person approval for deletion jobs beyond automated job flows.

If you want formal language for the DPA, Ben and Marissa can insert the bullets above into the DPA exhibit and provide the deletion-manifest format. If you need anything stricter (shorter retention windows, longer proof retention, or a no-store commitment), let's document that as a contract change and we'll route to Product/Legal for feasibility and pricing.

Thanks — I can also join a call with Alan and Procurement if that helps finalize the exhibit.

Kimberly Park
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
